prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: rear-end collision in Sugar Land, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported concussion. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1172; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was stopped at a red signal in the left lane of a major roadway in Sugar Land, Texas, when the rear of the vehicle was struck by a sedan operated by Driver 2. Driver 2 told me the brakes were applied too late on a wet pavement surface and admitted the impact was his responsibility. Two independent witnesses at the intersection gave statements that matched this account, and both said the collision occurred just as Driver 1 described. Photographs taken at the scene show a crushed rear bumper, a displaced trunk lid and a cracked tail lamp assembly, damage consistent with the speed and direction of the impact. I found no indication of prior body damage or repairs to the vehicle. The Passenger was seated in the front right position and was confirmed by both Driver 1 and the witnesses as present during the crash. Driver 1 reported a head injury and was transported for evaluation with symptoms consistent with a concussion. Driver 1 is listed as a named insured on the policy covering the vehicle.
